title: Minimum Swaps to Group All 1's Together
statement: `data` is an array whose entries are all `0` or `1`. A swap exchanges the values stored at any two positions of the array (they do not have to be next to each other). Return the smallest number of swaps after which every `1` of `data` sits in one unbroken run of consecutive positions; the run may be anywhere in the array. If the `1`s already form one run, or there are none, the answer is `0`.
notes:
## Intuition

Suppose there are `ones` ones in total. After grouping, they fill some block of exactly `ones` consecutive positions. Every `1` already inside that block can stay; every `0` inside it must be swapped with a `1` from outside, and one swap fixes exactly one such `0`. So the cost of a block is the number of `0`s in it, which is `ones` minus the `1`s it already holds.

The brute force tries each block and counts its zeros in O(n·ones). A sliding window of fixed width `ones` gets every block's count of `1`s in O(n).

## Approach

1. Count `ones`, the total number of `1`s; this is the window width.
2. Slide `right` across the array, adding `data[right]` to `inWindow`.
3. Once the window is wider than `ones`, subtract the value that just left it, `data[right - ones]`.
4. Track `most`, the largest `inWindow` seen.
5. Return `ones - most`, the zeros in the best block.

## Example 1, step by step

`data = [1, 0, 1, 0, 1]` has `ones = 3`. The windows of width 3 are `[1, 0, 1]`, `[0, 1, 0]` and `[1, 0, 1]`, holding 2, 1 and 2 ones, so `most = 2` and the answer is `3 - 2 = 1`: for instance, swap the `0` at index 1 with the `1` at index 4.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass to count, one pass to slide.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- Swaps are between any two positions, not adjacent ones, so the cost is a count of zeros, not a sum of distances.
- The window width is the number of `1`s, not a value you search for.
- With no `1`s at all, `ones = 0` and the formula gives `0` without a special case; the early partial windows never exceed a full one, so they do not distort `most`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ones` | total number of `1`s, also the window width |
| `right` | index of the newest position in the window |
| `inWindow` | number of `1`s in the current window |
| `most` | largest `inWindow` over all windows |

narration.3: Walk through every entry once to count the 1s.
narration.4: Each 1 adds to ones; the grouped block will be exactly this long.
narration.9: Slide the right edge of the window across the array.
narration.10: The new position joins the window.
narration.11: Once more than ones positions have entered, the window is too wide.
narration.12: Drop the position that slid out on the left.
narration.14: Remember the window holding the most 1s.
narration.16: Each 0 inside the best window needs one swap, so that is the answer.
